newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns French minister's charge on Africa.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns French minister's charge on Africa.

text.p: The United States sharply criticised a French government minister on Friday for saying an African trip by Secretary of State Warren Christopher was politically motivated ahead of the U.S. presidential election.
"These are outrageous, unfounded and unjustified remarks by a minister of the French government," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"I don't know if he's been living under a rock or what. He hasn't been paying attention to what the United States government has been doing," Burns added.

Commenting on Christopher's trip, Jacques Godfrain, French junior minister for cooperation, said on Wednesday: "I am delighted that Africa becomes a priority for the American government a few weeks before the presidential election."
He said the trip followed a cut in U.S. aid for Africa and he noted that President Bill Clinton had not visited the continent during his four years in office.

Burns said he could not imagine that either President Jacques Chirac or Foreign Minister Herve de Charette "knew about these remarks or sanctioned them" and said Washington was asking the French government for an explanation.
He added: "Just in their last meeting Secretary Christopher and Foreign Minister de Charette agreed to make Africa an area of intensified bilateral cooperation."

He noted that Vice President Al Gore had travelled to Africa and said Clinton's national security adviser Anthony Lake was an Africa expert who had brought commitment and action to U.S. policy toward the continent.
"We have made Africa a priority. We have argued with the Congress for more money for Africa," he said.

African Americans make up about 12 percent of the U.S. electorate and polls indicate about 80 percent of them will vote for Clinton in the Nov. 5 election. The polls put him comfortably ahead of Republican challenger Bob Dole overall.
Christopher, who had already stopped in Mali and Ethiopia, was travelling from Tanzania to South Africa on Friday before flying home via Angola on Monday.
